newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mostly lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mostly lower Thursday after another session of narrow ranges in the bullion market overnight.
With further Fed interest rate rises seen likely this year, the dollar remaining firm and equity markets stabilizing again, there was little incentive for investors in precious metals, traders said.
Nevertheless, many analysts still see gold as forming a bottom for the year near $340 an ounce, a level which has held twice in recent months.
COMEX June gold was called unchanged to off $0.50 from Wednesday's close of $343.30 after trading from $343.30 to $342.30 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted early around $340.50/$341.00 against the London morning fix of $341.15 and the New York close Wednesday of $341.10/60.
COMEX gold stocks rose 7,955 ounces Wednesday to 951,106 ounces, while silver stocks rose 426,103 ounces to 189,512,634 ounces.
COMEX May silver was called unchanged to down 1.0 cent from the previous close of $4.725.
NYMEX July platinum was called unchanged to off $0.50 from Wednesday's close of $374.40, with NYMEX June palladium called unchanged to up $0.50 from the prior close of $155.00.
